metadata.title: Red Sea Maritime Disruption Replay
metadata.subtitle: Fictionalized OSINT-style scenario
metadata.disclaimer: Mocked and curated sample data shaped like open-source feeds. This scenario is fictionalized for product validation and does not fetch live sensitive data.
metadata.region: Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb, Gulf of Aden

chapters.title: Commercial traffic reroutes
chapters.summary: The replay opens with merchant vessels adjusting speed and spacing through the southern Red Sea. AIS-like tracks, patrol aircraft, and satellite collection windows are shown as separate evidence layers.

chapters.title: Warning area expands
chapters.summary: Representative maritime advisories push traffic east of the normal corridor. A patrol aircraft begins an overwatch loop while a container ship diverts toward the Gulf of Aden.

chapters.title: Uncrewed aerial contact reported
chapters.summary: A short-lived aerial track appears near the shipping lane. The incident marker is intentionally non-attributional and exists to validate synchronized event storytelling.

chapters.title: Damage assessment window
chapters.summary: Satellite and maritime layers converge after the disruption. Analysts can scrub backward to compare vessel movement, air patrol coverage, and reported incident timing.

notes.text: Bulk carrier slows southbound transit and holds wider separation from nearby traffic.
Mocked advisory polygon increases perceived risk near the Bab el-Mandeb approach.
Uncrewed aerial contact reported near a commercial vessel track; no attribution is modeled.
Maritime patrol aircraft begins repeated east-west search legs across the shipping corridor.
Low-resolution collection pass crosses the incident area for post-event cueing.
Diverting vessel continues toward a safer anchorage while traffic density shifts south.
